blocks.h2: The Emergencies We See in Arlington Heights
blocks.intro: Most emergency calls from Arlington Heights homes fall into a few groups, and most of them are tied to the age of the housing and the weather.

items.body: In July 2011, almost 7 inches of rain fell in just over three hours and many basements filled through their floor drains. Heavy storms still bring backup calls. See [sewage backup service](/arlington-heights/sewage-line-backup-services).

Pipes in exterior walls, over garages and on outdoor spigot lines freeze first in a Cook County cold snap. When one splits, the leak usually starts when it thaws. See [burst pipe repair](/arlington-heights/burst-pipe-repair).
Many homes here are on their second or third water heater. When a tank lets go, it can put dozens of gallons on the basement floor. See [water heater repair](/arlington-heights/water-heater-repair).

items.h3: Old Shutoff Valves That Won't Close
items.body: In older homes, the main valve may not have been turned in decades. If it won't close in an emergency, we replace it so the next one is easier to stop.

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How fast can you get to my home in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: Call any time. We'll give you a realistic window and get there as soon as we can.
items.answer: Call us any time, day or night. Our office on East Central Road keeps our plumbers close to Arlington Heights. Arrival times depend on the day and call volume, but we'll give you a realistic window and get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: What should I do while I wait?
items.preview: Shut off the water at the nearest valve or the main. For gas, get out first.
items.answer: Close the valve closest to the problem or shut off the main. Keep people and pets away from sewage and from water near electrical outlets. If you smell gas, leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.

items.q: Where is the main water shutoff in my house?
items.preview: Usually in the basement where the water line comes through the wall, near the meter.
items.answer: In most Arlington Heights homes, it's in the basement where the water line enters, near the meter. Turn it clockwise to close. In an older home, test it before you need it, because old valves can stick.

items.q: Do you charge more for nights and weekends?
items.preview: You get the price before any work starts, whatever the hour.
items.answer: Whatever time you call, the plumber gives you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost before you agree to it.

items.q: How much does an emergency plumber cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and what it takes to fix it. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
